key_insight: A modified moving reference frame (mMRF) smoothly blends rotation rate to remove interface discontinuities, giving MRF-like efficiency while better preserving local flow continuity around propellers.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical middle ground for ship self-propulsion CFD, improving propeller-hull interaction fidelity without the cost of fully motion-resolving sliding interfaces.
method: Scale the reference-frame angular velocity with a spatially varying decay function from the propeller region to the stationary domain.
Derive and implement the modified governing equations in the RANS solver FreSCo+.
Verify on Taylor–Couette flow and apply to open-water propeller and Japan Bulk Carrier self-propulsion cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement in integral propulsion quantities and shows that mMRF reduces interface discontinuities and non-physical local artifacts, especially at large MRF fractions, at essentially the same computational cost.
watch_item: The decay function and interface placement must be chosen carefully, since the added smoothing can alter local kinematics if the transition region is not well tuned.
paper_title: A Modified Moving Reference Frame Method for Propeller Resolution
